title: fix: pasted chat images keep the wrong aspect ratio until remount
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: pasted chat images keep a padded 3:2 frame until the conversation is remounted, even after their actual dimensions are available.

## User Impact

Single-image previews immediately use the image's aspect ratio and retain it after returning from Settings or reloading. Very wide and tall previews remain bounded without distortion, and their file actions remain reachable. No configuration changes or migration are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The mounted frame deliberately froze its initial dimensions. It now derives geometry from the existing image presentation owner, using decoded dimensions only when durable upload dimensions are absent. The frame has one dedicated Solid component; no new cache or state owner is introduced. The obsolete untrack allowance and minimum-height letterboxing are removed.

The simplification pass retained the existing resource owner and moved its frame rather than introducing a parallel renderer. Production changes add 47 net lines for reactive geometry and reachable extreme-ratio actions; regression tests add 125 net lines.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the native clipboard paste/send problem against an isolated real Gateway: the 1200 × 563 image remained in a 3:2 frame before the fix.
- Replayed native ClipboardItem paste → send → upload receipt → Settings/back → reload. The patched surface stayed 400 × 187.65625 pixels at every stage. Only model inference used a synthetic loopback provider; clipboard, Gateway, media materialization, history, and browser rendering were real.
- 30 Chromium image-geometry cases, 55 image consumer tests, and 6 browser/Gateway end-to-end cases passed. UI build, TypeScript, targeted lint/format, stylesheet lint, and controller guards passed.
- Independent Codex P0–P2 review: no actionable findings. Its review covered the supplied patch, not executed tests; the live evidence above is from the implementation session.
- Previous-head CI run [40419236001](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40419236001) completed with one inherited failure: `Gateway status with native account identity > keeps shared chat usable without polling operator-only surfaces` expected no operator-only requests but received `board.get` at `gateway-status.e2e.test.ts:63`. The same test and assertion fail in scheduled main [40413333913, job 121889752226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40413333913/job/121889752226); PR failure is [job 121909881637](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40419236001/job/121909881637). Shard numbers differ. This is not an image-rendering flow. All other non-aggregate CI jobs, including `security-fast`, passed or were skipped. That attribution does not establish CI success for the review-repair head; its current checks are evaluated separately.

### After

### Review repair: short panoramas

ClawSweeper identified a real action-layout regression: a 1200 × 30 image retained a natural-ratio surface shorter than its 44px menu, allowing the menu to cover the following preview. The outer frame now reserves the menu footprint only when those file actions exist; the image surface keeps its ratio. The new browser regression fails on the reviewed head (next preview top 23.6875 < menu bottom 44) and passes with this repair. All 30 geometry cases and the 5 image-loading E2E cases pass again; canonical production UI typecheck (`pnpm tsgo:ui`), targeted lint/format, stylesheet and controller checks pass. An extra editor/test-wide `tsc` invocation reported untouched native-desktop bridge and quota-reset declaration errors; it is not reported as passing. These screenshots show the actual production-component browser fixture, not the real-Gateway clipboard capture above.

Before

![Before: short-panorama menu overlaps the next preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50886a49-a3c1-40de-8b4a-f34a579237cb)

After

![After: outer layout reserves the menu footprint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c92e822b-549c-478d-838f-ede92027181d)

### Prior-head CI investigation

Run [40422570301](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40422570301) ended cancelled: [checks-ui-e2e (3/7)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40422570301/job/121920939099) exceeded its 25-minute job deadline; 63 jobs completed successfully or skipped; the downstream CI gate failed. The job annotation confirms the timeout, but its logs are absent from both the job endpoint (BlobNotFound) and full run archive, and no timeout diagnostic artifact was uploaded. `pnpm test:ci-failed 185154` selected no Vitest failure. This is not green CI and its cause remains unproven.

Replayed the exact CI checkout `056271de0e84b393c07e1940a6d71bc114d2a783`, include set, 3/6 Vitest shard, and four workers in an isolated local checkout with locked dependencies: 53 files/222 tests passed; the two-large-PNG case in `chat-outbox-capacity.e2e.test.ts` failed with reversed attachment bytes. That same focused test fails on the actual CI main parent `f27bfa85c993fc64964cb19220d55f0934d7dd3e` (two other cases pass), establishing a pre-existing local ordering defect—not the cause of the logless CI timeout. Local execution also reported file-watcher EMFILE warnings, so it is not claimed as CI-equivalent passing proof. Original image-ratio and panorama checks remain passing.

### CI repair: attachment ordering

The reproduced two-large-PNG failure is now repaired. Native browser tracing showed the preview reconciling read membership from a stale attachment prop: after the first read completed, its ready slot was removed and later appended behind the second slot. The preview now uses the existing live composer accessor before reconciliation; no new state or order owner is added.

The focused regression fails before the repair with `[second.png, first.png]` and passes afterward. All 28 attachment consumer tests pass (1.61s file duration; 8.46s wrapper wall), as do all 20 mocked-Gateway E2E cases across capacity and read-lifecycle files (83.10s including UI build). The three capacity cases preserve exact ordered durable, transport and displayed bytes; large byte comparisons now emit bounded boolean failures instead of multi-megabyte Base64 diffs. Canonical `pnpm tsgo:ui`, three-file type-aware lint, formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Independent Codex P0–P2 review of this repair reports no actionable findings. The prior logless CI timeout is not retrospectively attributed to this bug; the repaired head has a fresh CI run.

A subsequent hosted test-type check caught the new cleanup callback returning Vitest utilities instead of void. The callback now discards that return value explicitly; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs --noEmit -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-chat.json` passes and all 28 attachment tests pass through `pnpm test` again. A direct, non-wrapper Vitest invocation also passed 28 tests but reported an Undici teardown exception; its run is not counted as passing, and the supported wrapper replay had no unhandled errors. This mechanical test-only correction does not change production behavior.

Thanks to @steipete for reporting the issue and requesting the fix.
